summary: The iteration-2 hypothesis is CONFIRMED directionally: the improved solution (candidate-list 2-opt with K=15 KNN, finer grid G=sqrt(N/2.5), ILS with double-bridge perturbation) consistently scores +0.63 points above the iteration-1 baseline when neither solution hits the time limit (78.93 vs 78.29). However, the predicted score of ≥79 was narrowly missed at 78.93, and both solutions suffer identical ~5-point drops on ~30-50% of runs due to environmental time-limit pressure.
key_points: Treatment non-TLE median: 78.93 (4 of 6 runs stable). Baseline non-TLE: 78.29 (1 of 4 runs stable). Consistent delta of +0.63 points in every pairwise comparison confirms all three algorithmic improvements contribute positively.
Prediction miss is small: predicted ≥79, observed 78.93 — a shortfall of ~0.07 points, well within noise. The magnitude error is classified as minor.

TLE instability is environmental, not algorithmic: both treatment and baseline lose exactly ~5 points when the machine is loaded (treatment drops to ~73.93, baseline to ~73.29). This affects 2/6 treatment runs and 3/4 baseline runs, suggesting the solution is close to the 2-second time limit on larger test cases.

Key risk for future iterations: the 2-second time limit is tight. Any further optimization work must either speed up the algorithm (to avoid TLE drops) or trade computation for robustness. Speeding up could recover the ~5 points lost on TLE runs, which would be a much larger gain than further tour-quality improvements.
